title: Per-tenant fastpath escrow and quota-aware demotion
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: During peak usage we need deterministic behavior that preserves enterprise SLAs while allowing free-tier and paid customers to continue using the service. Current tier routing uses coarse preemption and best-effort demotions which causes noisy neighbor effects and adversarial bursts that exhaust plan credits unpredictably.

Goal: Implement a per-tenant fastpath escrow that reserves a small, time-boxed execution budget (escrow) for high-priority lanes (enterprise, paid) for immediate admission, plus a quota-aware demotion strategy that gracefully routes excess free-tier requests to lower-cost model variants or delayed execution slots rather than hard-dropping or immediate regional fallback. The system should reduce tail latency for enterprise customers, keep free-tier degradation graceful, and expose metrics for cost and user-observable errors.
acceptance_criteria: Enterprise-tier p95 latency for standard generate calls does not regress more than 5% during 10x free-tier overload tests
Under synthetic credit exhaustion, free-tier request success rate drops gracefully (>=50% progress via lower-cost model variants or queued-delayed-responds) instead of abrupt 100% failures
Escrow logic can be configured per-tenant and per-route via console flags and respects plan-defined budgets
Fallback to lower-cost model variant preserves structured output format (for code/chat/JSON outputs) for 95% of sampled prompts
Dashboard surfaces escrow utilization, demotion rates, and cross-tier spillover with <30s freshness
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight per-tenant in-memory escrow that maintains a small token balance (time-windowed) used to grant immediate fastpath admission for high-priority requests. On admission, the request consumes escrow tokens; tokens replenish at a configurable rate tied to the customer's plan. When a lane is saturated or escrow is empty, apply a quota-aware demotion pipeline: 1) check for compatible lower-cost model variants in the same region; 2) if available, attempt immediate reroute with model-compatibility shim (ensures function-call/structured output compatibility); 3) if no variant available or demotion budget exceeded, enqueue into short-delay window (50-500ms) to wait for KV-batching opportunities; 4) if delay window overflows, return a soft-degrade response explaining the demotion and offering a retry or upgrade link. The prioritizer will additionally implement a gentle token-decay so long-running bursts slowly reduce fastpath capacity instead of instant preemption. Configuration will be exposed via policy objects in the control plane and TLS-authenticated per-tenant overrides in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Console: policy editor and preview for per-tenant escrow (owner: console-ux)
Observability: add escrow/utilization, demotion events, variant-success metrics (owner: observability)

Rollout: staged canary with traffic shaping and kill-switch (owner: SRE)
rollout_plan: 1) Internal feature-flagged rollout on a small set of test tenants; 2) Canary on a single region with synthetic load to validate p95 and demotion behavior; 3) Gradual ramp by tenant cohort (enterprise only -> paid -> free) with monitoring alerts; 4) Post-mortem and tuning window before full global enablement. At any point the control plane kill-switch will revert to previous preemption logic.
testing_plan: Unit tests for escrow arithmetic and decay; integration tests validating admission and demotion paths; compatibility tests ensuring function-calling and structured-output preserved when routing to variant models; chaos tests introducing regional overload and delayed KV cache responses; long-running soak to check token drift and memory usage.
migration_plan: Default per-tenant escrow disabled. Existing plan objects will get a computed default escrow profile on next plan mutation. Admins can opt-in to enable per-tenant overrides. For Dedicated/Private, include a migration tool to backfill escrow state from plan usage history.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect token math could starve paid customers. Mitigation: conservative defaults, canary, and automatic rollback on SLA breach.
Risk: Variant model may return incompatible structured outputs. Mitigation: strict compatibility matrix and automated sample validation before routing.
Risk: Additional runtime state increases memory pressure. Mitigation: bounded in-memory escrow with LRU eviction and persistent snapshotting for Dedicated deployments.
Risk: Adversarial tenants trying to game escrow. Mitigation: anomaly detection and enforcement policies with throttles and penalties visible in console.
Risk: UX confusion for free users seeing degraded responses. Mitigation: soft-degrade messages with upgrade/feedback links and telemetry to evaluate user impact.
